precedents.quote: the resolved path must exist and be a REGULAR FILE — a symlinked pin is DRIFT (the pin must bind bytes, not a name).
an EMPTY pins[] array is DRIFT `pins-empty`, not CLEAN: a registry that binds nothing is precisely the state this gate exists to catch.
A bare-directory token (.ufo/waves/round-63) is not a resolvable citation — `git ls-tree -r --name-only` lists blobs, and naming a directory is not naming a committed file.

gap.attack: the pinned object need not be an instrument: git show <rev>:<path> prints link text for a mode-120000 symlink and a listing for a mode-040000 tree; auth_findings hashes it and compares to the receipt's own declared digest, so a receipt pinning a directory or a data blob authenticates
